=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py:reconcile() lines 268-300 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: When any created item is rejected, all created roots are moved to quarantine but legitimate created roots are never restored.
  WHY: A legitimate file created alongside a prohibited file is stranded in quarantine, causing the reconcile to fail and discarding valid model work.

- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:main() lines 326-342, _load_issue_label_map() lines 167-185 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The offline issue-label map covers only the current and tracking issues, so references to other issues are treated as lookup failures and unlisted tracking-issue violations can evade detection.
  WHY: PR creation may be blocked with a misleading lookup error, while `Fixes` references to unmapped orchestrator-tracking issues are not classified.

- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py:_is_ignored() lines ~166-178 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `_is_ignored` treats `git check-ignore --no-index` exit code 128 in a workspace without `.git` as a fatal error.
  WHY: Scratch or partial workspaces fail closed with exit 20 instead of completing reconciliation.

- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py:lines 166-176 (_is_ignored function) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_is_ignored` classifies force-added tracked files matching `.gitignore` patterns as ignored.
  WHY: Legitimate tracked files can be quarantined and omitted from the changed-path manifest.

- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py:lines 89-105 (_inventory walk function) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `os.scandir` permission errors are converted into a fatal `GuardError` for the entire workspace walk.
  WHY: One inaccessible directory aborts reconciliation and blocks otherwise legitimate model output.

- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py:_inventory() and _digest() lines ~80-115 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The guard recursively walks and hashes the entire workspace at every snapshot and reconciliation attempt.
  WHY: Repeated full-tree scans compound across retry loops and can exceed per-attempt budgets in large repositories.

- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:lines 67-72 (run_resolver_validator_python function) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `run_resolver_validator_python` invokes the sandbox helper without checking that it exists and is executable.
  WHY: A missing helper produces an opaque execution error instead of the clear diagnostic used by sibling validator wrappers.

- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py:line 256 (hidden-path rejection rule) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The hidden-path rule rejects tracked `.ai/`, `.claude/`, and similar configuration directories because only `.github` is excluded.
  WHY: Legitimate files under tracked pipeline directories can be quarantined.

- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh:line 414 (workspace-guard ReadWritePaths property) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `ReadWritePaths=${workspace} ${runtime_dir}` splits paths containing whitespace.
  WHY: A whitespace-containing runtime directory can lose write access to quarantine and cause reconciliation to fail.

- .ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt:line 225 (added entry) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The manifest lists `changelog.d/4290-security-boundary-hardening.md`, while the created file is `changelog.d/post-agent-python-startup-isolation.md`.
  WHY: The manifest contains a nonexistent entry and omits the actual changelog fragment, causing filesystem validation drift.

- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh:`case "${role}" in validator|workspace-guard` block lines ~26-35 and the `provider_required` gating through the rest of the script | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The intentional credential-check bypass for `validator` and `workspace-guard` roles is not documented inline.
  WHY: A future maintainer could reintroduce universal credential handling and expose `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to validator roles.

- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:lines 67-72 (run_resolver_validator_python) | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `run_resolver_validator_python` follows the naming pattern of sibling validator wrapper functions without colliding with an existing symbol.
  WHY: The reviewer reported this as a naming and backward-compatibility observation, not a runtime defect.

  Line or code reference: lines 268-289 (reconcile created_roots restoration logic)
  Problem: When any change is rejected, all created_roots are moved to quarantine at lines 268-270, but only rejected non-created items are further processed in the else branch at lines 280-289. Non-rejected created roots (legitimate new files created in the same model run) are never restored and remain stranded in the quarantine directory.
  Why it fails at runtime: A model that creates both a legitimate new source file and a malicious sitecustomize.py would have both files quarantined; the legitimate file is lost, the guard exits 20 (blocked), and the caller retries with no knowledge that a legitimate file was created.
